Ossify

/OS-uh-fye/ - rhymes with classify · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Ossify means to become rigid and stop changing.

The chef worried that the menu had begun to ossify: the 'seasonal specials' had not changed in four years.

Worked Example

Grandpa's morning route had ossified decades ago — the same bench, the same crossword, the same two slices of rye — and the family learned that even a new toaster counted as an upheaval.

Ossify is literally 'to turn to bone,' and the figurative sense keeps that image: habits, institutions, or opinions that were once living and flexible harden until they cannot bend without breaking.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

harden: to grow firm or unyielding, literal or figurative

fossilize: to become a relic — outdated as well as unchanging

calcify: to stiffen with mineral deposits; figuratively, to grow inflexible

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

adapt: to change to fit new conditions

evolve: to keep developing over time

Where it sits · how far past change it has gone — harden → ossify → fossilize

harden vs. ossify: Habits can harden and still be broken with effort; hardening is the milder, earlier stage of what ossify completes.

fossilize vs. ossify: Fossilize goes further than ossify: the ossified rulebook still runs the club, while the fossilized one survives only as a curiosity from another age.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — oss-

Root — oss-: bone (Latin os, ossis)

Suffix — -ify

Suffix — -ify: to make, to become

Put it together

Put it together: Latin os, ossis means 'bone,' and -ify means 'to make or become': ossify is literally 'to become bone.' Anatomists still use it that way — an infant's soft cartilage ossifies into a skeleton — and the figurative sense borrows the picture: whatever ossifies has traded its flexibility for bone.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Latin os, 'bone,' survives in English almost nowhere outside the anatomy lab — ossuary, a chamber for storing bones, is its rare other descendant — so there is no everyday relative to lean on. The familiar half is the suffix: -ify, 'to make,' the same maker that builds mollify, vilify, and stupefy in this unit.

Word Building

Word Choice

formal / written

Ossify is the pointed choice for institutions, rules, and thinking that have stopped being able to change — it diagnoses, where 'harden' merely describes. Its unit-mate mollify makes a neat opposite pair to remember: one word softens, the other turns to bone.
